edition: Andrew D. Huberman with Jessica Wapner, Protocols: An Operating Manual for the Human Body (2026). Official UK sample: Cornerstone Press, ISBN 9781529921281 hardback / 9781529921298 trade paperback.
scope: Exact ready 22-pair selected reading of the introduction, Sleep Protocols 1–3 and authorized Personal Growth Protocol 1. Not all seven domains, the full operating manual, a published RU translation or a treatment plan.

essential.assessment: 10 pairs read continuously in RU and EN. The declared sleep/light/attention selection runs from a mechanism-based habit premise to sleep and the light clock, actual morning/afternoon/evening actions, and an actual attention-return procedure. The cover makes the selection clear; no all-seven-domain, treatment or guaranteed-outcome promise. The brief attention transition is understandable in this scope.

core.assessment: 16 pairs read continuously in RU and EN. Adds the introductory purpose, real study/recovery experience, eye caution, daytime/nighttime loop, attention transition and imperfect-attention qualification. These remain connected to the author’s selected account rather than an independent coaching program.

deep.assessment: 22 pairs read in order in RU and EN. Adds the real skateboarding recollection, cloudy-day/window and pre-sunrise contingencies, explicitly partial buffering, phone-study qualification and the author’s start/stop observation proposal. No invented case or imported podcast procedure found.

currentSafetyEfficacyCheck.method: Targeted primary research, original expert consensus and current primary agency/clinical guidance for claims actually retained. Not a systematic review or validation of the book bundle.

claimChecks.actualClaim: Sleep affects attention, mood and recovery; daylight can help organize sleep/wake timing.
claimChecks.locator: NIH/NHLBI How Sleep Works; Why Is Sleep Important?, opening and Problems with thinking and memory.
claimChecks.assessment: The broad background is consistent with current agency guidance. This does not independently validate every selected protocol or a causal personal outcome. No correction needed.

claimChecks.actualClaim: Retinal light timing affects circadian timing; author suggests 30–60 minutes after waking and 5–10 minutes in clear daylight, with evening dimming.
claimChecks.locator: Brown et al., PLOS Biology 2022, abstract, Expert consensus-based recommendations, Additional considerations and response-duration/variability rationale.
claimChecks.actualAccess: Read those primary consensus sections directly; this is the panel’s report, not a new trial.
claimChecks.assessment: Supports stronger daytime and dimmer evening/night light, while dose depends on intensity, spectrum, duration and individual sensitivity. It does not establish a universal 5–10-minute dose. Its evening recommendation begins at least three hours before bed; candidate accurately reports Huberman’s one-hour heading without claiming that one hour is sufficient or independently validated. No materially false efficacy claim asserted; do not silently replace the book with the panel’s program.

claimChecks.actualClaim: Author attributes only partial buffering against subsequent artificial light to prior afternoon/evening light; dimming still needed.
claimChecks.locator: Te Kulve et al., Scientific Reports 2019, DOI 10.1038/s41598-019-52352-w, abstract and experiment description.
claimChecks.actualAccess: Read the primary abstract: randomized crossover, 12 young women, 2.5-hour early-evening bright exposure, acute physiological/sleepiness measures. Nature full-page fetch failed; no full-paper claim.
claimChecks.assessment: There is experimental support for prior-light modulation under specific conditions, not proof that a short sunset walk prevents health harms. Candidate already attributes, limits to partial effect and retains dimming; it asserts no numerical protection or health guarantee. No correction required.

claimChecks.actualClaim: Daylight exposure does not require sun staring; eye conditions/sensitivity warrant ophthalmology advice.
claimChecks.locator: ARPANSA The sun and eye damage; MedlinePlus Photophobia, Considerations, Home Care and When to Contact a Medical Professional (reviewed April 29, 2025).
claimChecks.actualAccess: Read relevant primary agency/clinician-reviewed medical guidance directly. AAO pages returned 403; search snippets were not treated as a read full source.
claimChecks.assessment: Direct solar viewing is a real injury risk, and clinical photophobia is a real reason to avoid forcing exposure and seek care. Those limits are already present. Candidate does not tell readers to remove protection or rely on blinking as proof of safety. No new hypothetical contraindications or warning checklist added.

claimChecks.actualClaim: General possibility of benefit from daytime light; no personal success guarantee.
claimChecks.locator: ENLIGHTENme, J Pineal Res September 2026, DOI 10.1111/jpi.70174, primary abstract; older adults, randomized self-directed light supplementation.
claimChecks.actualAccess: Read primary record, abstract and displayed figure descriptions; not full paper.
claimChecks.assessment: Recent evidence retains the importance of real-world exposure and adherence; it is not a test of Huberman’s short outdoor routine. It supplies no basis to turn the candidate into a proven treatment. No contrary finding requiring a narrow correction to an asserted candidate claim identified.

claimChecks.actualClaim: App-recorded mind wandering was associated with lower happiness; author recommends periodic re-anchoring.
claimChecks.locator: 2010 study record/abstract; authorized excerpt study discussion and final procedure.
claimChecks.actualAccess: Primary abstract and authorized text only.
claimChecks.assessment: The digest preserves association and subjective self-reports while identifying the practical step as the author’s proposal. It makes no universal causal claim, mental-health cure claim or treatment-execution promise. No correction needed.

currentSafetyEfficacyCheck.result: No material unsupported or outdated health claim requiring correction identified within this explicitly attributed, non-guaranteed selected account. Author fidelity and scientific validation are distinguished. Real eye-risk qualifications are retained; no hypothetical warning program added.

PubMed 12390501 open supplied no substantive text. Search result was discovery only; no full-paper assessment based on it.

sourceSufficiencyAssessment: Actual consulted chapter pages and an authorized procedure excerpt support the declared selection. Scope is visible in the bilingual title/description, cover and Sources; it does not claim all seven domains or a full manual. Omitted domains are outside the promise, not silently reconstructed from podcasts/newsletters. This is enough for this candidate; no whole-edition/source-completeness gate applied.
substantiveParityAssessment: All 22 RU/EN titles/bodies, bilingual metadata, method/source notes and all cumulative routes read. Steps, times, quantities, real autobiographical cases and qualifications agree. The retained procedures are the author’s, including the two attention-return steps and start/stop self-observation. No material translation mismatch, invented scene or new compiler program found.
